extracted.intended_audience: security teams, CISOs, incident responders, IT managers, and organizational leaders responsible for enterprise security
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style postmortem of the 2017 Equifax breach that distills concrete security requirements and operational best practices organizations should follow to prevent similar incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patch Faster
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an up to date asset inventory of all systems and their software versions; set SLAs for patching critical vulnerabilities (24-48 hours for actively exploited CVEs); verify patches are actually applied, not just scheduled. The page emphasizes that CVE-2017-5638 had a patch available for two months before the attack and that failing to apply it enabled the breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat vulnerability management as critical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat vulnerability management as critical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run regular vulnerability scans; treat unpatched critical systems as incidents; track patches and remediation status, and ensure remediation processes are operational and auditable rather than merely tracked on a schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor Your Security Tools ("monitor your monitoring")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security tools only work when they’re functioning; Equifax's monitoring was disabled by an expired SSL certificate. Set alerts for expiring certificates months in advance; monitor that your security tools are actually functioning; build dashboards that show tool health (not just detections); run regular tests to verify detection capabilities work; alert on monitoring gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set alerts for expiring certificates and verify decryption pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Set alerts for expiring certificates months in advance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SSL/TLS certificates that enable decryption/inspection do not expire unnoticed; validate decryption/inspection pipelines so monitoring tools can inspect encrypted traffic. The expired certificate at Equifax prevented network monitoring from decrypting exfiltrated data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement network segmentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement network segmentation between systems with different sensitivity levels so attackers cannot easily move laterally; assume a breach will happen and design systems to limit lateral movement; avoid placing all sensitive assets on a single flat network where credentials on one system grant broad access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not store credentials in plaintext; use secrets management
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never store credentials in plaintext anywhere; use a secrets management system; rotate credentials if you find they’ve been leaked or if you suspect compromise. Equifax attackers found plaintext credentials that unlocked sensitive databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement Zero Trust controls
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require multi-factor authentication for all sensitive system access; implement least privilege so compromised accounts have limited reach; monitor for unusual access patterns even from authenticated users. Zero Trust reduces the effectiveness of stolen or reused credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice incident response and prepare communications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run tabletop exercises; have pre-approved communication templates; know who makes decisions before a crisis hits; use clear, non-confusing consumer-facing domains and messaging (Equifax created confusing/parody-like sites); avoid response choices that waive consumer legal rights. Practice reduces delays, confusion, and poor public-facing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect exposed credentials via dark web monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch for your credentials on the dark web
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dark web monitoring to detect employee or organizational credentials that appear in third-party breaches and hacker forums so you can reset them before attackers exploit reuse; many attacks start with credentials leaked in prior breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify detection and response timelines; minimize discovery gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize time-to-detection and verify detection capabilities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and test end-to-end detection and response timelines (Equifax had a 78‑day dwell time); ensure tools detect exfiltration and lateral movement; set processes to rapidly investigate alerts and act on them; treat monitoring failures as high-priority incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational controls on privileged actions (insider/exec behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage executive and insider actions during incidents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have policies and controls governing insider trading, executive communications, and information handling during active incidents; ensure clear governance so sensitive knowledge (e.g., discovery of a breach) does not enable improper trades or actions that compound legal/regulatory harm.
